citation: Commission on Chicago Landmarks. Clarke House: Chicago's Oldest Building. Chicago: Commission on Chicago Landmarks, 1983; revised 1996 (Michael Soet, revision editor). Prairie Avenue House Museums.
author: Commission on Chicago Landmarks (staff)
locator: 'The Construction and Style of the Clarke House', pp. 2-5: 'They modeled the house in the Greek Revival style'; 'A columned portico, or porch, topped by a triangular roof shape, or pediment, was the most prominent feature'; the style 'flourished in America from about 1820 to 1860'.
rights_note: A city commission's publication with photographs by Bob Thall and the Chicago Historical Society; cited in text only, nothing reproduced.
access_notes: Retrieved and read 2026-10-17 (the PDF also circulates in the Internet Archive's City of Chicago Landmark Designation Reports collection).
note: Names the Clarke House's style: it was built in 1836 for Henry B. and Caroline Clarke and 'modeled ... in the Greek Revival style'. The house was designated a Chicago Landmark on 4 October 1970. It was built the year after the 1835 scene date, so it stands in no scene of this project; it is the style library's Chicago example of a style the 1835 town knew.
what_it_supplies: that the Clarke House is Greek Revival, and the style's defining columned portico and pediment
the Clarke House's 1836 date and its 1872 move
what_it_does_not_supply: any image this project may reuse
